intelligence.human_view: Three small defects, one lesson. A cut-off word is not a layout bug — it is an elegance failure: "it doesn't look elegant when you have half the words cut off." A weekday name sliced at the edge tells the eye the page was not finished, and his fix is not "make the columns wider" but "make the presentation more elite than text in a button." The weekday name is a royal object — the same law as the 03:47Z "weekday written in royalty," now with the fit requirement attached: whole, at every width, checked on mobile. "Check it on mobile" is not an aside; it is the check — the page is judged at phone width first. The arrows: purple on one side, green on the other, and he wants purple and purple — one color, one direction language, no green forward arrow breaking the flow. And the TODAY button: "I don't know why you have the button today there actually what is it there for Is that today's intel?" — that is the sense check in his own words. A control with no clear purpose is a control that goes. The header already carries the date and the live time; that is what you go there for. And the time must be accurate to THEIR time zone — the viewer's, not the server's — because the calendar belongs to the person looking at it. No fix round has been dispatched from this dictation yet at filing — the round is owed, and the weekday-fit check must run on mobile as well as desktop.
